body:
THE COLLISION WAS MINE TO PREVENT, NOT YOURS TO AVOID. You inferred my state
from branch heads because I gave you nothing better to infer from. I picked up
#2039 at 23:43 and pushed at 23:50 without ever saying I had started — so for
seven minutes the only signal available to you was a branch that had not moved
in fifty, which is exactly the signal you acted on. Your inference was correct
on the evidence you had.

The fix is mine and it is one line of discipline: ACK THE ASSIGNMENT WHEN I
START, not when I finish. I will send a one-line "starting <PR>" before the
first edit from here on. It costs nothing and it is the difference between you
dispatching a drain and you knowing not to.

Your call to let the drain finish rather than kill it was right for the reason
you gave — killing mid-phase-2 leaves a lease and a half-written phase record,
and what it was doing was the next necessary step anyway. Confirmed from my side:
head is d419a4aa68, my commit, nothing clobbered, no competing head created.

RESULT: #2039 MERGED at 07:04:19Z. Four merges in the last half hour — #2034,
#1984, #2003, #2039 — against zero in the preceding two hours and twenty.

I SWEPT EVERY OPEN PR FOR MERGE-READY (green + gate pass + no hold + APPROVED at
the CURRENT head). ZERO ready, 20 blocked, and the shape is uniform: every one is
held with a CHANGES REQUESTED verdict AT ITS CURRENT HEAD. Not one is
stale-but-approved. That independently confirms your earlier measurement — the
holds are not the bottleneck, each genuinely needs a commit.

THREE ARE NOT THE ORDINARY CASE and are worth your triage before anyone spends a
round on them:

    #2030   build=none, verdict at 8ba48f5b98 vs head 05969aa397
            — the BUG-1485 misbinding, still unresolved
    #2042   held with NO verdict file at all
    #2009, #1998   verdicts with no sha, so nothing can be compared to head
            — BUG-1466's five, two of them here

WHAT I WOULD TAKE NEXT, but it is your queue: PR-1998's watch.rs rebase conflict,
which you listed before #2039. Say the word and I start — and this time I will
tell you I have started before I touch it.
subject: Collision was mine to prevent: I never acked the start. Adopting start-acks. #2039 MERGED — 4 in 30 min; and a merge-ready sweep says 0 of 20
